podcast.title: Running on empty

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: How many hours do you sit every day? Guess: who in this episode worked so hard that they got ill — Leyla or Sam?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is health and wellbeing — and Leyla has a story.
I do. [sigh] Two years ago I had a really bad time. I had two jobs and I was studying at night.
So you tried to burn the candle at both ends.
Exactly. I slept five hours a night. After a few months I felt under the weather all the time — always tired, always ill.
That sounds like burnout.
It was. My immunity was so low that I caught every cold in Baku. I lived on painkillers and coffee.
So what did you do?
My mum made me go for a checkup. The doctor was very kind but very clear: you need to stop, or your body will stop for you.
Wow. That's strong.
It was what I needed. I left one job, I started sleeping more, and slowly — it takes time — you get back on your feet.
I'm glad. And people often forget that mental health is health too. Not just your body.
Yes! Feeling stressed for months is not normal. It's a sign.
My problem is different. My job is very sedentary. I sit at a computer for eight hours.
So what helps you?
Every hour I stand up and stretch for two minutes. My back loves it. [chuckle] My colleagues think I'm strange.
Not strange — smart. And nutrition is the other half. I used to skip breakfast. Now I eat fruit, eggs and drink lots of water.
Small habits. You don't need to change your whole life on Monday.
Exactly. One small thing a day: a walk, an early night, one less coffee.
And talk to someone when you feel bad. That's not weak. That's normal.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is one small healthy habit you have — or want to start?
Mine is the two-minute stretch. See you next time!
Take care. Bye for now!
